newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian oil exporters want fewer 'state' exports.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil exporters want fewer 'state' exports.

text.p: Russia's Union of Oil Exporters said on Wednesday that the government should cut the amount of crude oil sold abroad under state-sponsored federal programmes.
Union director Anatoly Yushkin said the government's 1997 target of 70 million tonnes under the programmes, or about 70 percent of the amount of oil Russia can export each year, was too high.
"We are not against the programmes per se -- it is the volumes in the programmes that must be reasonable," he said.
Federal programmes authorise companies to buy crude oil at domestic prices and export it. Both the state and the companies, which include traders as well as producers, realise profits.
There are about 20 decrees calling for federal programme oil exports of up to 70 million tonnes this year.
A battle has broken open between producers and traders over who should have the right to carry out federal programmes.
The Union's deputy director, Yevgeny Samoilov, quoted by Interfax news agency, said volumes under the programmes should total about 25 million tonnes year.
